name: XL1509-ADJE1
title: XL1509: 2 A, 150 kHz, 40 V input buck DC-DC converter
summary: A step-down regulator with its power switch on chip, running at a fixed 150 kHz from 4.5 V to 40 V and delivering up to 2 A. It comes in fixed 3.3 V, 5 V and 12 V versions and an adjustable version (XL1509-ADJ) whose 1.23 V feedback threshold sets an output from 1.23 V to 37 V with two resistors. Compensation is internal, the duty cycle reaches 100 %, and an active-low ON/OFF pin with hysteresis shuts it down; current limit with frequency foldback and thermal shutdown protect it. Package is SOP8L.

notes: The code reads XL1509, then the version (ADJ, 3.3, 5.0 or 12), then E1. E1 marks the lead-free, RoHS-compliant part, supplied on tape and reel. The marking ID is the same string as the part number.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Supply input, 4.5 V to 40 V DC. Decouple it to GND with a capacitor large enough to keep noise off the input.

pins.name: OUTPUT
pins.function: Switch output (SW): the switching node that delivers power towards the output through the inductor.

pins.name: FEEDBACK
pins.function: Feedback (FB). Takes the output voltage, scaled by a resistor divider outside the chip, for regulation; its threshold is 1.23 V.

pins.name: ON/OFF
pins.function: Enable, active low: low runs the regulator, high shuts it down. Left open it reads low.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground. Keep it off the return between the Schottky diode and the output capacitor, where switching current spikes would induce noise in the part.

circuits.title: Typical application, 12 V to 5 V at 2 A
circuits.description: The 5 V fixed version running from 12 V and delivering up to 2 A. The internal switch drives the OUTPUT pin; L1 and COUT filter the switched node into the output, and the 1N5820 Schottky D1 carries the inductor current during the off time. FEEDBACK connects straight to the output. CIN is the bulk input capacitor and the 1 µF C1 sits beside it at the supply pin. ON/OFF is the control input: held low the converter runs, taken high it stops.

parts.note: low runs the regulator, high stops it

circuits.title: 3.3 V version, 12 V in, 3.3 V at 2 A
circuits.description: The 3.3 V fixed version stepping 12 V down to 3.3 V for loads to 2 A. Compared with the 5 V circuit the inductor drops to 47 µH and the output capacitor rises to 330 µF; the 1N5820 freewheel diode, the 470 µF input capacitor and the 1 µF ceramic stay. FEEDBACK goes directly to the output node, and ON/OFF low enables the part.

circuits.title: 12 V version, 24 V in, 12 V at 2 A
circuits.description: The 12 V fixed version converting 24 V to 12 V at up to 2 A. The input capacitor is a 50 V part and the freewheel diode is the 30 V 1N5821; the 68 µH inductor and 180 µF (25 V) output capacitor form the output filter. FEEDBACK is wired to the output, and the part runs while ON/OFF is low.

circuits.title: Adjustable version, 24 V in, 5 V at 2 A
circuits.description: The adjustable version set for 5 V from a 24 V supply. R2 (3.1 kΩ) from the output and R1 (1 kΩ) to ground divide the output down to the 1.23 V feedback threshold, so VOUT = 1.23 × (1 + R2/R1). The 3.3 nF CFF across R2 is the feed-forward capacitor. L1 (47 µH), COUT (470 µF) and the 1N5821 Schottky make up the power stage; CIN and the 1 µF C1 bypass the input, and ON/OFF low turns the part on.

circuits.title: Standard test circuit, fixed output versions
circuits.description: The circuit the fixed versions' output voltage and efficiency are measured in. It is the basic buck stage: input capacitors CIN and C1 at VIN, the switch output into L1 with freewheel diode D1, COUT at the output, and FEEDBACK taken from the output. An optional second LC stage (3 µH and 180 µF) after the output further cuts ripple at the load.

operation.text: A step-down converter with its power transistor on chip, under fixed 150 kHz PWM control. Its duty cycle adjusts linearly from 0 to 100 %, and its minimum dropout is 1.5 V. Frequency compensation and the oscillator are internal.

An internal 3.3 V regulator and 1.23 V reference feed an error amplifier on FEEDBACK, whose output is compared against the 150 kHz ramp to set a latch that drives the output switch, a Darlington NPN pair from Vin to OUTPUT. Switch current is sensed across a 44 mΩ resistor in the Vin path by two comparators with thresholds of 200 mV and 220 mV. A start-up block driven from ON/OFF and a thermal shutdown block also act on the driver.

The fixed versions carry the output divider inside: R1 = 2.5 kΩ from the error amplifier input to ground, with R2 = 4.2 kΩ (3.3 V), 7.6 kΩ (5 V) or 21.8 kΩ (12 V) up to FEEDBACK. On the ADJ version R2 is 0 and R1 is open, so FEEDBACK goes straight to the error amplifier and an external divider sets the output from 1.23 V to 37 V.

ON/OFF is active low and TTL compatible, with hysteresis: the part turns off when the pin rises past about 1.4 V and back on when it falls below about 0.8 V. An open pin is taken as low, so the regulator runs. In shutdown the supply current is 80 µA typical.

The switch current is limited (4 A typical with FEEDBACK at 0 V), and a second current limit level drops the switching frequency from 150 kHz to 50 kHz when it trips. Thermal shutdown is built in, and power dissipation is internally limited.
R1, from FEEDBACK to ground, is about 1 kΩ and a 1 % part for best stability. R2 then sets the output by VOUT = 1.23 × (1 + R2/R1).

CFF sits across R2. Outputs above about 10 V require it; typical values are 100 pF to 33 nF, given by CFF = 1/(31 × 1000 × R2). It adds stability at high output voltage, at small input-to-output difference and with output capacitors of very low ESR such as solid tantalum. Ceramic, plastic and silver mica types are suitable; Z5U ceramic is not recommended because it is unstable.
CIN and the optional C1 (1 µF) both sit close to pin 1 and pins 5 to 8, to improve stability and keep input line noise down.

The heavy-current paths (input capacitor, VIN, OUTPUT, the diode, the output capacitor and their ground returns) are kept short over a ground plane. The divider resistors go next to FEEDBACK on short leads, and the feedback trace stays clear of the inductor's field. The GND pins sit outside the ground path between the Schottky diode and the output capacitor.

operation.topic: Choosing L1, COUT and the diode
operation.text: For the fixed versions the inductor and output capacitor are picked from the selection table by output voltage and highest input voltage, at 2 A load; for the ADJ version the output capacitor and feed-forward capacitor are picked by output voltage. The catch diode is a Schottky from the diode table whose reverse voltage equals the highest system input voltage.
